transcript:
Header: 2026-04-29 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Diego (CS), Ava (Product); Dr. Laura Kim, Priya Nair, Samir Vyas, Ethan Brooks (Helix Genomics)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, I see we have the core team from helix, appreciate the time. quick agenda — nail down success criteria, share what workloads look like, and sketch a benchmark and cost model that fits your budget.
00:18 Dr. Laura: yep thanks. our use case is a genomics explainability assistant embedded in our analyst UI. typical interactions are conversational but often return 400-1,200 tokens in the response. concurrency is modest — 10–30 active analysts — but bursty during triage windows.
00:40 Maya: got it. when you say 400–1,200 tokens, is that total tokens (prompt + response) or response only?
00:47 Priya: response only; prompts are usually 50–200 tokens. we showed some examples in the meeting invite but we'll upload canonical sets.
00:56 Jordan: perfect, that helps. two immediate knobs that move cost/latency: batching and caching — prefix caching for repeated context (like sample histories) and continuous batching at the runtime level. we also want to discuss quantization — int8/4 tradeoffs for accuracy vs throughput.
01:12 Samir: our budget for a month-long pilot is around $12k all-in, and we'd like to know what that buys in throughput and latency. we also need to keep raw patient data inside our VPC for logs — so private deployment or dedicated with VPC peering is preferred.
01:31 Diego: quick note — security side will validate SOC2 docs and retention policies, Ethan will lead that.
01:37 Ethan: yes i'll send a list but we need to confirm that no raw genomes leave our VPC and logs can be configured to redact PHI.
01:46 Maya: we can run the POC in a dedicated pool in your VPC (private control plane) and enable customer-managed KMS; Redwood has a private deployment flow that matches that. there are perf differences vs hosted — dedicated generally gives more predictable throughput and allows larger batch aggregation while avoiding cross-tenant tail latencies.
02:05 Priya: what's the typical per-token delta between hosted and dedicated?
02:10 Jordan: depends a lot on model and quantization. rough thumb: hosted (multi-tenant) best-case you might see slightly higher per-token billable due to software overhead, but you get a managed baseline. dedicated can reduce per-token cost by 10–30% in many cases because you control batch size and can run more aggressive kernels; with int8 quant we often see 30–50% TCO improvement at the cost of some accuracy risk.
02:35 Samir: we care about p95 latency — ideally <300ms for a single-turn explainability query. is that realistic with 1k token outputs?
02:44 Maya: 300ms p95 for 1k tokens is tough. we'd expect 300–600ms p95 on optimized dedicated infra for streaming-friendly models; if you need synchronous single-call 300ms p95, we should consider model distillation or output chunking / early-first-token strategies. also KV/prefix cache can shave 10–40% of compute if a lot of the prompt is shared.
03:12 Priya: accuracy regression guardrails are important. we need to detect hallucinations or unacceptable drift compared to our internal baselines. can Redwood tie quality monitoring to the benchmark?
03:21 Ava: yes — we have Redwood Optimize eval hooks. for the pilot we suggest a small eval set (50–100 canonical prompts) and regression thresholds; we'll flag tokens-per-inference and perplexity-like metrics plus human review for edge cases.
03:36 Jordan: for cost modeling we typically ask for three numbers: expected monthly active users (or calls/day), average prompt tokens, average response tokens, and desired SLOs. then we produce per-1k-token estimates under different configs: hosted baseline, dedicated fp16, dedicated int8 + KV cache enabled, etc.
03:58 Samir: rough numbers: 20 active analysts, each 15 sessions/day average, so ~300 sessions/day. prompt avg 150 tokens, response avg 800 tokens — roughly 285k tokens/day or ~8.5M tokens/month.
04:23 Jordan: good, that gives us a starting point. budget $12k/month — we need to show per-token cost that keeps pilot under that. assuming naive hosted (no caching) with current open models, cost might be $0.004–0.008 per 1k tokens (placeholder), but with Redwood batching and KV cache and dedicated quant we can approach $0.0008–0.002 per 1k tokens depending on kernels and model size.
04:55 Priya: those numbers vary a lot; what are the main levers you tune during the POC?
05:01 Maya: main levers: quantization (fp16 -> int8/4), batch size/latency SLO tradeoff, KV/prefix cache hit-rate, sequence length caps and token truncation policies, and routing to cheaper model variants for low-risk queries. we also run a production-like workload through a bench harness to measure real batching gains — synthetic numbers often mislead.
05:23 Samir: can you demo the bench harness? even a small run would help us believe the model.
05:28 Jordan: yes — Maya will share a link to a harness that runs locally or in your VPC and uploads results; it reports throughput, p95/p99 latency, and effective tokens-per-second plus cost estimate per run.
05:40 Priya: timeline — we want pilot in prod-ish environment within 4 weeks. is that feasible?
05:45 Maya: feasible if we lock prompts and access and your sec team approves the deployment. typical timeline: week 1 collect prompts and sample data + run initial hosted baseline; week 2 dry-run benchmarks and iterate on configs; week 3 dedicated pilot deployment and main benchmark runs; week 4 analyze results and present unit-econ recommendations.
06:09 Dr. Laura: success criteria from our side: (1) p95 latency <400ms for 80% of sessions, (2) pilot TCO < $12k/month, (3) no security exceptions (SOC2 red flags), (4) quality regression within defined threshold vs internal model.
06:30 Jordan: we'll map those to measurable metrics: p95 latency numbers per config, cost per 1k tokens, and a small eval suite pass rate.
06:40 Ethan: security question — how are logs handled in dedicated? can we redact at ingestion?
06:46 Maya: yes, logs can be routed to your collector on-prem or to a private s3 bucket; Redwood supports redaction hooks and customer-managed KMS. we'll include the SOC2 whitepaper and redaction patterns in the follow-up.
06:58 Samir: can we try a hybrid: hosted for dev + dedicated for pilot?
07:03 Diego: that's a common pattern — dev in hosted for fast onboarding, pilot in dedicated with identical model versions, then scale to prod dedicated or private.
07:12 Priya: one more: what about model variants for quality vs cost — do you support automatic fallback?
07:18 Ava: yes — smart routing can route requests based on policy (latency priority vs cost priority) and fallback to higher capacity model or region. that's something to validate during the bench.
07:30 Jordan: ok to recap — deliverables: cost workbook + bench harness link (Jordan/Maya), customer provides prompt sets and token distributions (Priya/Samir), security list (Ethan), schedule bench runs week of 2026-05-11, align success criteria next week.
07:55 Dr. Laura: thanks — we'll prioritize prompt sets and security list. looking forward to the workbook.
08:02 Jordan: great — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the 2-hour bench window and attach the cost sheet. any other Qs?
08:09 Priya: not right now.
08:12 Maya: thanks everyone.
08:15 (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hears ("key vee cache" heard at times), speaker overlap occasional. Bench harness reference: https://redwood-internal.s3/bench/helix-harness (demo link, access controlled). Cost workbook: https://redwood.app/sheets/unit-econ-template (shared on follow-up).
